title: LinearDesign: more stable mRNA sequences designed by an algorithm
summary: The algorithm, based on a parsing technique from natural-language processing, finds the most stable mRNA sequence for a given protein in about eleven minutes. According to Baidu’s press release, whose study appeared in Nature, sequences produced this way showed greater stability, protein expression and antibody response than comparators in animal experiments. Figures are company-reported; the Baidu release copy on EurekAlert was reviewed, not a baidu.com page.

evidence.tested: LinearDesign-designed mRNA for COVID-19 and VZV was compared with wildtype and codon-optimized sequences in animal experiments, measuring half-life, expression and antibody response; the figures are company-reported and the release describes no independent replication.
evidence.unknown: The Nature abstract states no specific study limitations and the release states none; the release says benefits such as lower doses and fewer side effects are possibilities not tested.
evidence.ai_role: A parsing-based algorithm (LinearDesign) optimized mRNA structural stability and codon usage for a given protein.
